ai.description: *Uperodon marmoratus* is a 3–4 cm globular frog. It is brown with distinct yellow or white spots and possesses a shovel-shaped metatarsal tubercle for burrowing.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uperodon marmoratus* is best distinguished by the distinct, bright white or yellowish marble-like spots scattered across its smooth, dark brown to purplish-grey back.
ai.habitat: *Uperodon marmoratus* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found in leaf litter at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Indian Dot Frog is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending much of its time buried underground to retain moisture before emerging to forage for termites and ants.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uperodon mormoratus* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in shallow, temporary rain pools or rock crevices. They exhibit explosive, aquatic breeding.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uperodon mormoratus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, occurring across Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Maharashtra at elevations of 200–1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Indian Dot Frog emits a rapid, high-pitched, insect-like trill or "peep" sound, typically heard emanating from water-filled rock crevices or leaf litter during monsoon.
